X2 concurred, trusting the veteran General's judgment.<ref name="ES-DS" /> Shortly thereafter, the Empire launched an [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|attack]] on Yavin 4, and the Rebel Alliance was able to destroy the Death Star when [[Rebel pilot/Legends|Rebel pilot]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] fired two [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedoes]] into a small [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|thermal exhaust port]] that triggered a chain reaction, resulting in the station's destruction.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I'm no Jedi now. Not since ''this''.''"<br />"''I don't need your eyes, just your mind. And everything you know about fighting the Empire.|Rahm Kota and the apprentice on Cloud City|<ref name="TFUvg" />}}
[[File:RahmKotaHS.jpg|left|thumb|Rahm Kota]]
Rahm Kota was a hardened soldier who was noted as being an excellent tactician and combat commander. Regarded as cold and militant by his fellow Jedi, Kota always advocated the use of aggressive force in punishing those who disrupted law and order. Nevertheless, Kota was loyal to the Jedi Order&mdash;despite his disagreement with some of their policies&mdash;and was committed to the stability of the Galactic Republic. He gained a reputation for never abandoning those in need,<ref name="TFUdb" /> and, during the Clone Wars, his leadership style instilled confidence in his troops. Yet, as the war dragged on, Kota came to the belief that the conflict would see the end of both the Jedi and the Republic, and he grew weary of seeing soldiers and trusted friends killed in battle.<ref name="TFUcg" />

During his enforced exile, Kota employed reckless tactics in an effort to draw out Darth Vader,<ref name="TFUn" /> although the missions were always well-planned.<ref name="TFUcg" /> Confident of his own abilities and skills, Kota was certain that he could face the Dark Lord and defeat him in single combat. Cocky to the point of arrogance, he was humbled when he was beaten and his sight was taken from him during his duel with Vader's secret apprentice, Galen Marek, over Nar Shaddaa.<ref name="TFUn" />

Following the loss of his sight while dueling Marek, Kota became disillusioned in his planned attempts at defeating the Empire, coming to believe that challenging the Emperor's vast war machine was a "fool's errand." Adopting a defeatist attitude, the aging General began to see the conflict in terms of numbers, stating that it did not matter how many stormtroopers were killed because there were thousands more waiting to take their place. His defeat at the hands of a "boy" shook his confidence, and Kota came to see himself as useless without his sight. His connection to the Force was severely weakened, and the General believed that he had been cut off from it, although he continued to demonstrate some abilities&mdash;such as probing Marek's thoughts on Cloud City to determine his intentions, and feeling the aftermath of the young man's experiences in his former home on Kashyyyk.<ref name="TFUn" />

During his time on Cloud City, Kota turned to drink to ease the loss of his sight and his Force connection, wanting nothing more than to be left alone and forgotten. Kota allowed his appearance to fall into disrepair; his usually immaculate hair was allowed to hang loose, his robes became stained, and he left dirty the bandages that covered his sightless eyes. Even after being recruited by Marek to assist in building a rebellion against the Empire, Kota often requested alcohol and became disappointed and withdrawn, since there was none available to him.<ref name="TFUn" />

[[File:Kota_vs_Starkiller.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Kota battles the apprentice just prior to sensing the young man's future.]]
Kota's journeys with Marek&mdash;and witnessing the apprentices' attempts to forge an alliance to bring down the Empire&mdash;helped him to rediscover his fighting spirit and confidence. By the time of the mission to destroy the shipyard over Raxus Prime, Kota began to act more like his old self, issuing orders again like the seasoned general he once was, and counseling Marek on how to use the Force to pull a Star Destroyer out of the sky&mdash;an act that the General, in his previous defeatist frame of mind, would have previously considered impossible. When Marek met with the three Senators to form the Rebel Alliance on Corellia, Kota appeared at the meeting having laid his ghosts to rest, being neat, sober, and confident&mdash;and with his connection to the Force seemingly reestablished when he was able to confidently walk to the meeting table as if he were able to see clearly. In a conversation with the other members at the meeting, he revealed that he considered the apprentice to have saved him.<ref name="TFUn" />

Kota always suspected that Marek was, in fact, the darksider who had blinded him. Nevertheless, he sensed that the dark side did not hold sway over Marek as much as the boy thought. Resolving to help him, even if he felt he could offer no practical assistance to the young man, Kota was confident Marek would do the right thing. He supported the boy through the assembly of the dissident Senators and was sure that Marek's arrival on the Death Star signaled his intent to start the planned rebellion.<ref name="TFUn" />

During his travels with Marek, Kota became a surrogate father to the young man, which surprised the battle-hardened General.<ref name="Insider 120">{{InsiderCite|120|Juno and the Jedi}}</ref> These feelings resurfaced a year later, when it appeared that Marek had returned from the dead, although the young man insisted that he was a clone of the original. Through the Force, Kota felt that this individual—who knew himself only as "Starkiller"—had the same presence as the apprentice and did not believe that he was a clone. Despite Starkiller's origins, Kota trusted him implicitly, noting that he knew both the best and the worst that the apprentice had done, and that he was willing to take his chances supporting him. Later, when Starkiller asked Kota directly about his belief that the young man was not a clone, the General admitted that it really did not matter to him. He was back, and that was all there was to it.<ref name="TFUIIn" />

[[File:Rahm_Kota_by_Brian_Rood.jpg|thumb|left|Rahm Kota, Jedi Master]]
Although the Jedi Order taught their members to let go of their hate and anger, for fear of being consumed by the dark side of the Force, Kota could not. His anger, hate, and impatience was often felt by other Force-users. Despite this, Kota never fell to the dark side, instead channelling his feelings to accomplish successes on the battlefield. The General was also perfectly willing to sacrifice forces to attain a strategic victory if the target was important enough.<ref name="TFUIIn" /> He had no compunctions about using the raw hatred and desire for vengeance against the Empire of the troops under his command to his advantage. He knew that it would make his troops more effective in battle against the enemy, although he was accepting of the fact that using them in this manner would mean high casualties.<ref name="TFUIIvg-db" />

Dedicated to the Alliance and focused on destroying the Empire, Kota believed that personal feelings and desires held no place in war. When he was rescued from Cato Neimoidia by Starkiller, the General's first instinct was to use the young man as a rallying point to galvanize the Alliance into making a major strike against the Empire.<ref name="TFUIIn" /> In this way, Kota was not unlike Vader in one respect&mdash;they both saw Starkiller as a tool that they could use to further their own agendas, albeit for different motives.<ref name="TFUII-digital">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]'' digital artbook</ref> When Starkiller placed finding Eclipse above helping the Rebellion, Kota became frustrated and reminded him that the galaxy was at war. Although he held little compassion,<ref name="TFUIIn" /> Kota did have a gentler side, which he displayed by comforting Eclipse on Kashyyyk following Marek's death on the Death Star,<ref name="TFUn" /> and by recognizing the fact that Starkiller loved Eclipse.<ref name="TFUIIn" /> Despite this, he also sometimes made decisions based on practicality rather than morality, such as sparing Vader on Kamino. Kota's actions were prompted by the potential advantage of having Vader as a prisoner, and not because killing an unarmed opponent would have been morally wrong.<ref name="TFUII-digital" />

As a member of the Rebellion, Kota returned to his role as a confident general, strongly believing that direct military action was necessary to keep the Alliance moving forward. He was dismissive of Mon Mothma's policy of developing the Alliance before striking and often assaulted Imperial targets without authorization from High Command. He kept his sightless eyes uncovered for the majority of the time<ref name="TFUIIn" /> but did wear a [[black]] cloth across his eyes on occasion. He was bold and proud to call himself a Jedi, even during a time when admitting that fact was tantamount to admitting he was a Rebel and opposed the Empire. Kota recruited and guided X2, a Force-sensitive former clone trooper, after sensing that he was strong in the Force, despite his personal feelings about clones lacking the necessary skills to be effective soldiers. This was partially done out of respect for his former Padawan, Falon Grey&mdash;who was the genetic template for X2&mdash;and because Kota felt the Force within X2.<ref name="ES-DS" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|Vader thinks he's turned you. But I can sense your future. And Vader won't always be your master. I sense only&hellip;me?|Rahm Kota sees a vision of the future|<ref name="TFUvg" />}}
[[File:Kota_saber.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Rahm Kota's lightsaber]]
Kota was a skilled lightsaber duelist and was a practitioner of the lightsaber combat form [[Form VII/Legends|Juyo]]. Despite being trained in the most aggressive of the seven forms of lightsaber combat,<ref name="TFUcg" /> Kota preferred to adopt a defensive stance in combat, using the Force to protect himself until he could launch a counterattack.<ref name="TFUdb" /> His prowess with the lightsaber also allowed him to block and redirect incoming blaster fire.<ref name="TFUcg" />

Kota was physically fit and capable of feats of acrobatics. He could use these in conjunction with his Force powers in combat, allowing him to slip past an opponent's defenses to strike them. Kota also employed charging at the enemy and attacking them with quick, rapid strikes in combat. He could also enhance his combat abilities with the Force, as well as using the Force to increase his [[Force jump/Legends|height and length of his jumps]] and his [[Force speed/Legends|speed]]. Kota could use the Force to [[Mind trick/Legends|affect the mind of others]].<ref name="TFUcg" />

Kota's connection to the Force allowed him to control his fear, and he was immune to any attempts to instil fear in him.<ref name="TFUcg" /> He could also use the Force to enter a meditative trance before employing his Force abilities to hone his skill and increase the effectiveness of its outcome.<ref name="Serenity">In ''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]'', Kota is noted to have the ability "serenity" in his roleplaying game statistics. The ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]'' explains the effects of this ability.</ref>

Well-trained in the use of the Force, Kota was able to use telekinesis to move objects or deflect incoming attacks and projectiles,<ref name="TFUcg" /> and to throw his lightsaber with extreme accuracy.<ref name="TFUdb" /> He was also able to use the Force to snatch both Galen Marek and Darth Sidious' lightsabers from them during his encounter with Imperial forces on Corellia and on the Death Star, respectively.<ref name="TFUn" /> He employed telekinesis to hurl objects at enemy combatants or repel them from his presence,<ref name="TFUdb" /> and had enough mastery to detach the command tower from the TIE Fighter Construction Facility over Nar Shaddaa and send it plummeting toward the planet.<ref name="TFUvg" /> He possessed training in farsight<ref name="TFUcg" /> and had received at least one vision of the future, during his duel with Marek, when he sensed his future and his opponent's would be intertwined. He was highly skilled in [[Force deflection/Legends|Force deflection]], which he easily used to catch Force lightning and a Force push from Marek during their duel.<ref name="TFUn" />

Despite the loss of his sight, Kota's connection to the Force enabled him to function as if he had not lost it. He was able to move and fight as well as an able-bodied individual, fly starships, and command major battles from the bridge of a starship. He would often react to events as if he was able to see them with his eyes and could tell where people were in relation to himself so that he could speak directly to them.<ref name="TFUIIn" /> Kota also possessed some skill in healing himself with the Force. After Kota's seven-day incarceration in the Tarko-se Arena on Cato Neimoidia, the medical examiner recorded that, despite several severe injuries, Kota was in no danger of dying and needed only quick treatment before returning to duty. The examiner also noted that Kota's body had evidence of many past injuries that had not been healed with conventional medical techniques.<ref name="TFUIIvg-db" />

Kota's abilities were not limited to his connection with the Force. He was fluent in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], and was trained in the use of light [[Armor/Legends|armor]] so that wearing it during combat did not hinder his movements or affect his combat capabilities. While the lightsaber was his primary weapon, Kota was also proficiently trained in the use of simple weapons. He was also well trained in how to access secure [[Computer/Legends|computer]] information and to defeat security systems.<ref name="TFUcg" />

==Equipment==
Kota wielded a [[Rahm Kota's lightsaber|green-bladed lightsaber]] in combat. The weapon was eventually taken from the general by Galen Marek after their duel at the TIE Fighter Construction Facility, who modified the weapon and used it as his own.<ref name="TFUvg" /> Kota eventually acquired another green-bladed lightsaber that was identical to his previous one and used it during his service to the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="TFUIIvg" /> Unlike most Jedi, who hung their lightsabers from their [[Utility belt/Legends|belts]], Kota kept his in a sheath on his back.<ref name="TFUvg" />

Kota wore a combination of [[Jedi apparel/Legends|Jedi robes]] and light combat [[Armor/Legends|armor]].<ref name="TFUcg" /> Following the loss of his sight, Kota sometimes took to wearing a cloth strip across his eyes.<ref name="TFUvg" /> He carried a [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]],<ref name="TFUcg" /> and during his time with the Rebellion made use of a personal starship.<ref name="ES-DS" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Cully_Fredricksen.jpg|thumb|left|Cully Fredricksen]]
Rahm Kota was introduced in ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'',<ref name="TFUvg" /> a [[2008]] multimedia project created by [[LucasArts]], in collaboration with [[Dark Horse Comics]], [[Del Rey]], [[The LEGO Group]], [[Hasbro]], and [[Palace Press]].<ref name="TFUmp">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (multimedia project)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' multimedia project]]</ref> Kota was one of the main characters and featured in [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed|''The Force Unleashed'' video game]],<ref name="TFUvg" /> [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|novel]],<ref name="TFUn" /> and [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (graphic novel)|comic]].<ref name="TFUc" /> Kota later gained mentions in source material publications, including ''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''<ref name="TFUcg" /> and ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''.<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> A toy was also made of the character, released as part of the ''[[Star Wars: 30th Anniversary Collection]]'' toy line.<ref name="30th">''[[Star Wars: 30th Anniversary Collection]]''</ref> In [[2009]], Kota was included in both the [[Wikipedia:PlayStation Portable|PSP]]<ref name="ES-PSP" /> and [[Wikipedia:Nintendo DS|Nintendo DS]]<ref name="ES-DS" /> versions of ''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Elite Squadron]]'',<ref name="ES" /> and ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed: Ultimate Sith Edition]]'', which was a release of the original game with several newly-added levels. While the majority of the new content in the ''Ultimate Sith Edition'' was [[Canon|non-canon]], the Jedi Temple level was first released as downloadable content and takes place within the storyline of ''The Force Unleashed''.As there is nothing to suggest that the level is non-canon, unlike the Tatooine and [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] levels, this article assumes it is part of the "proper" storyline.<ref name="TFU-USE" /> In [[2010]], a [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II|sequel]] to ''The Force Unleashed'' was released, and Kota was once again a main character.<ref name="TFUIIvg" /> His role was expanded on in both the [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (novelization)|novelization]]<ref name="TFUIIn" /> and the [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (graphic novel)|comic]].<ref name="TFUIIc" />

Kota is voiced in ''The Force Unleashed'' [[Star Wars video games|video game]] and its sequel by actor [[Cully Fredricksen]], whose likeness was also used as the basis for the character's appearance. Fredricksen was the first actor cast for the game. One of several actors who read for the part,<ref name="CCCP">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/videogames/news/f20070918/index.html|text=Casting and Capturing Captivating Performances}}</ref> Fredricksen felt the audition was akin to a theatrical audition, as he was given a longer time to prepare for the role than he would have had if he were reading for a film part. LucasArts also provided Fredricksen with the script, character breakdown, and concept artwork of Kota before the audition.<ref name="Insider 120" /> Fredricksen approached the reading fully in-character, which initially made the casting director believe that the actor may be standoffish and difficult to work with. However, it was soon realized that Fredricksen was just ''being'' Kota.<ref name="CCCP" /> Fredricksen, however, had a different take on the audition, believing that he had not "walked in as Kota." Impressed by the team at LucasArts and how seriously they took ''The Force Unleashed'' project, Fredricksen felt that the team wanted him to succeed, and their attitude made him comfortable during the process. The actor felt that the team was able to bring Kota out of him, remarking that "it was like the collaboration had already begun before I was ever given the part." Fredricksen later told his wife that the audition had been one of the most gratifying he had ever attended.<ref name="Insider 120" />

Fredricksen's convincing audition, combined with the actor's physicality and his ability to produce a wide range of facial expressions, convinced the production team to hire him as the gruff General. Fredricksen was described as the "consummate professional," and "a lot of fun to work with."<ref name="CCCP" /> Fredricksen enjoyed making the game, believing that the collaboration of the actors and crew was vital to the project, since they were all eager for it to succeed and to produce the best game they possibly could. One element that Fredricksen positively commented on was the fact that, during recording sessions, the entire cast for that scene would record their lines together, allowing them to act against one another. This was in contrast to other voice-over recording sessions Fredricksen had been involved in, where he had just delivered his lines by himself with the director reading for the other characters. This method allowed for more believable chemistry between the characters.<ref name="Insider 120" />

Kota, as portrayed in the video game version of ''The Force Unleashed''&mdash;both in-game and in promotional shots&mdash; has [[brown]] eyes.<ref name="TFUvg" /> In the novel of ''The Force Unleashed'', however, his eyes are referenced as blue just prior to the apprentice blinding him with their locked sabers.<ref name="TFUn" />

===Alternative storylines===
[[File:RahmKota-TFU.png|thumb|right|Rahm Kota]]
In the [[Wikipedia:Wii|Nintendo Wii]], PSP, and [[Wikipedia:PlayStation 2|PlayStation 2]] versions of ''The Force Unleashed'', Kota is found in a [[The Undertow|bar]] on Nar Shaddaa instead of Cloud City. Also, as Marek receives the vision of his father following the completion of the [[Jedi Trials/Legends|Trial of Spirit]] in the ruins of the Jedi Temple on Coruscant rather than in his former home on Kashyyyk, he attempts to discuss his experience with Kota prior to the mission to the Wookiee homeworld. Kota is not interested in talking about it, however.<ref name="TFU-alternate" /> In the [[Wikipedia:Cell phone|cell phone]],<ref name="TFU-cell">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''&mdash;[[Wikipedia:Cell phone|cell phone]] version only</ref> [[Wikipedia:N-Gage|N-Gage]], and [[Wikipedia:iPhone|iPhone]]/[[Wikipedia:iPod Touch|iPod Touch]] versions of the game, Kota is killed by Marek during their encounter on the TIE Fighter Construction Facility.<ref name="TFU-alternate2">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''&mdash;[[Wikipedia:N-Gage|N-Gage]], and [[Wikipedia:iPhone|iPhone]]/[[Wikipedia:iPod Touch|iPod Touch]] versions only</ref> In the cell phone version, Marek states that Kota "fell into the chasm," although this is not shown in the cutscene.<ref name="TFU-cell" /> In the N-Gage/iPhone/iPod Touch versions, Marek Force-chokes Kota to death following their duel. The storyline then continues without Kota's involvement.<ref name="TFU-alternate2" />

In the game, despite losing his lightsaber to Marek following their duel aboard the TIE Fighter Construction Facility, Kota still has one when he joins the apprentice on Cloud City. During the level, Kota can engage and fight Imperial soldiers while following the apprentice. He also has the lightsaber during the cutscene when Vader interrupts the Corellian meeting and uses it to try and fight the Dark Lord.<ref name="TFUvg" /> In the novel, Kota loses his lightsaber during the duel on the TIE Fighter Construction Facility, and it becomes Marek's own. Part of the plot of the novel involves Marek further refining the weapon to become better attuned to himself. This article assumes that the novel version of events take precedence over the game events and that Kota did not have a lightsaber following his duel with Marek on Nar Shaddaa.<ref name="TFUn" />

Due to the different depictions of Kota's actions during ''The Force Unleashed'' that are presented in the various console versions of the game, this article complies with the [[Lucasfilm]] statement that the novel is the definitive "true story."<ref name="TFU bookshelf">{{SWArchive|url=vault/books/news20080819.html|text=''The Force Unleashed'' on your Bookshelf}}</ref> This article presents a consolidated account wherein events in all versions of the game are incorporated as long as they do not conflict with the canon established in the novel.

===Alternate dark side endings===
At the conclusion of ''The Force Unleashed'', the player has the option of two paths to follow to complete the adventure. The branch point comes directly after the duel with Darth Vader aboard the Death Star; there, the player has the choice to either face Vader again, killing him, or engage the Emperor in a duel to save Kota, who is being electrocuted with Force lightning. The canonical ending involves fighting the Emperor and saving Kota. If the player takes the option to kill Vader, however, the Emperor attempts to sway the apprentice back to the dark side by persuading him to kill Kota. The apprentice attempts to strike the Emperor down instead but is beaten back. With the apprentice down, the Emperor uses the Force to pull the ''Rogue Shadow'' into the observation dome in which they are located. The resulting explosions and debris kill all those present, including Kota.<ref name="TFUvg" />

Like ''The Force Unleashed'', the sequel game also offers a choice of endings. After Starkiller has beaten Vader on Timira City, the option is given to either spare Vader and take him prisoner, or to succumb to the dark side and kill him. If the dark side option is taken, Starkiller goes to strike Vader down, only to be impaled by a red lightsaber wielded by [[Dark Apprentice|another clone]] of Galen Marek. This clone had succeeded in overcoming his emotions and becoming the apprentice that Vader desired. As Starkiller falls, Kota engages the Dark Apprentice in a brief lightsaber duel. The General is slashed during the fight, then lifted into the air and Force-choked. The Dark Apprentice then casts him back toward the Rebel troops who accompanied him, before he uses the Force to push them all off the platform and into the [[Ocean/Legends|ocean]] below.<ref name="TFUIIvg" />

===Conception and creation===
[[File:Concept_kota.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Concept art of Kota by Amy Beth Christenson]]
{{Quote|If anything Kota only became tougher because Cully Fredrickson ''[sic]'', who plays him, is so big and imposing, and he came in already in character.|W. Haden Blackman|<ref name="Co-Star Evolution">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/videogames/news/f20071031/index.html|text=''The Force Unleashed'': Co-Star Evolution}}</ref>}}
During the development of ''The Force Unleashed'', once the concept of having the player control a character that was Darth Vader's secret apprentice was settled on, it was realized that Jedi opponents would be needed for him to go up against. Concept art for various Jedi was drawn up, including one that was described as a "[[Wikipedia:Samurai|Samurai]] Jedi." At the same time, the production team was looking to add a character who would act as a second mentor to the apprentice, one who could give him instruction in the Force that he could not receive from Vader. Originally, the concept called for the disembodied spirit of [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], preserved in the [[Netherworld of the Force/Legends|Netherworld of the Force]], to fulfill this role. However, [[George Lucas]] did not approve of this concept, since he wanted a completely new cast of characters for the game,<ref name="Co-Star Evolution" /> and a living mentor of flesh and blood.<ref name="art">''[[The Art and Making of Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref>

Ideas for the character were explored, including a hermit Jedi in the tradition of Yoda, and even bringing back the character of [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]] in some form. However, in order to streamline the process, it was decided that the mentor role would be filled by one of the Jedi opponents originally designed for the apprentice to face early on in the game. [[W. Haden Blackman]], the project lead on the game, and the production team decided that they wanted a Jedi who was different from the established Jedi Master mentor characters already established in the ''[[Star Wars]]'' universe. Instead of the mystic Jinn, or the nurturing Obi-Wan Kenobi, the mentor was meant to be "less [[Wikipedia:Gandalf|Gandalf]] and more Army General."<ref name="Co-Star Evolution" />

Concept artists [[John Stafford]] and [[Richard Davis]] explored the character's appearance and possible background having in mind his survival through the Great Jedi Purge, coupled with his Samurai-like sense of honor. After years of hiding and surviving in isolation, the character would be "hard-boiled": bitter, betrayed, hardened, insensitive, scarred, traumatised, damaged or amputated; even a bit paranoid and verging towards the Dark Side. His experience would be reflected on his disheveled appearance, dented armor and tattered clothes.<ref name="art" /> Rahm Kota's blindness was inspired by the Japanese fictional character [[Wikipedia:Zatoichi|Zatoichi]], a blind masseur and samurai.<ref name="Zatoichi">{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/715421587072090113|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=Is Kanan now a reference to Rahm Kota? No, but they both owe a debt to Zatoichi, a character every SW fan should know about. #StarWarsRebels|archivefile=File:Tweet_pablohidalgo_kanankotazatoichi.jpg}}</ref>

Artist [[Amy Beth Christenson]] returned to the original concepts and found the artwork of the Samurai Jedi. She redesigned the character, creating one who was [[Armor/Legends|armored]], wore a topknot, and carried his lightsaber on his back. In addition, he was scarred from combat. The original concept art went through several revisions but did not evolve much from the original drawing.<ref name="Co-Star Evolution" />

With the basic appearance of the character established, the script evolved and it was decided that he would be one of the Apprentice's adversaries from the start, allowing thus more development and character arc. John Stafford wanted the character to be wounded after this meeting<ref name="art" /> and a downfall was introduced. This played into the concept of the [[Wikipedia:Ronin|Ronin]]&mdash;a samurai who has lost everything that he once held dear, such as his master, his honor and duty, and sense of worth&mdash;and Kota was shown to be at his lowest point, becoming a drunkard, feeling worthless, and unable to use the Force. His experiences with the Apprentice help Kota to regain his pride and connection to the Force, in turn returning him to the path of the Jedi. When Fredricksen was cast in the role, Blackman noted that the character actually became tougher than originally scripted due to the actor's imposing physical stature.<ref name="Co-Star Evolution" />
